title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: A multiple never tells you whether a stock is cheap or expensive until you know how much future cash flow is already baked into today’s price.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Principle

web_blocks.text: What ₹305.90 Already Prices In: Reverse DCF & Forward Earnings Math

web_blocks.html: On November 13, 2026, Kross closed at ₹305.90, giving a ₹1,970.44 Cr market cap [23]. It trades at 28.42x TTM earnings (29.1x on Screener) and 3.77x book value of ₹81.10 per share [1][23]. That price sits 103.2% above its ₹150.52 52-week low and 6.28% below its ₹326.40 52-week high after a +51.06% three-month rally [23]. Q2 FY27 drove that re-rating: sales jumped +79.6% YoY to ₹235.1 Cr and PAT rose +143.5% YoY to ₹19.69 Cr [3]. That lifted TTM sales to ₹822 Cr and TTM net profit to ₹69 Cr [1].

A Reverse DCF shows what buyers at ₹305.90 must believe. Enterprise value sits near ₹2,060 Cr (₹1,970.44 Cr market cap plus ₹119 Cr September 2026 debt, net of cash) [1][23]. At a 12.5% cost of capital and 5.0% terminal growth rate, ₹305.90 prices in 16%–18% yearly sales growth through FY32. It also assumes EBITDA margins rise from 12.1%–13.0% to 15.0%–16.0%, with working capital under 85 days [1][14]. Given -₹111 Cr of FY24–FY26 free cash flow, the price leaves slim room for delays in February–March 2027 seamless tube trials [9][11].

web_blocks.takeaway: On the post-Oct 30, 2026 fully diluted base of 6.75 Cr shares (6,60,09,422 basic + 15L promoter warrants = 6,75,09,422), Base Case FY28E PAT of ₹108 Cr yields ₹16.00 EPS and a ₹400.00 target at 25.0x. From ₹305.90, Base Case upside (+30.8% to ₹400.00) equals Bear Case downside, yielding a 1.00:1 reward-to-risk ratio against the ₹212.00 stop. Waiting for ₹268.00–₹282.00 improves Base Case asymmetry to 1.69:1.

web_blocks.text: Head-to-Head Peer Comps: Paying Up for Growth Over Capital Efficiency

web_blocks.html: Peer comps show why entry price matters right now [26][27]. Jamna Auto trades at 23.0x Screener P/E (25.46x TradingView TTM) with 26.0% ROCE, 22.3% ROE, 12.8% OPM, and a 1.68% yield [26]. GNA Axles trades at 17.19x TTM P/E with 14.3% ROCE, 0.19x debt-to-equity, and +23.06% TTM sales growth [26]. Happy Forgings trades at 52.58x TTM P/E on a 25.30% OPM [27]. Ramkrishna Forgings trades at 77.3x TTM P/E after margins dipped to 8.69% [27].

web_blocks.caption: Indian CV, Axle & Forging Peer Comparison (Verified Nov 13, 2026 Snapshot)
web_blocks.takeaway: Kross trades at a P/E premium to both Jamna Auto (25.46x) and GNA Axles (17.19x) despite lower ROCE (16.4% vs. Jamna Auto 26.0%) because its +35.86% TTM sales growth and +79.6% Q2 FY27 surge price in seamless-tube margin expansion.

web_blocks.company: GNA Axles Ltd (FY18–FY20 Commercial Vehicle & Tractor Cycle)
web_blocks.mechanism: Like Kross, GNA Axles entered a truck upcycle with strong OEM approvals and new capacity. When US Class 8 builds and Indian M&HCV sales cooled in FY19–FY20, sales and margins fell together and its P/E shrank.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: GNA Axles fell over 55% from its 2018 peak to its 2020 low as P/E dropped from ~22x to single digits. It later recovered to 17.2x TTM P/E in Nov 2026 on ₹2,496.64 Cr market cap and 14.3% ROCE.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Peak earnings times peak P/E multiples create sharp downside when freight slows. Buying Kross near support instead of chasing +51% rallies guards against multiple compression.

web_blocks.html: Working-capital speed also explains why Kross sits below Happy Forgings (52.58x TTM P/E, 25.30% OPM) yet above GNA Axles (17.2x TTM P/E at 14.3% ROCE) and near Jamna Auto (23.0x Screener P/E at 26.0% ROCE) [26][27]. Defending a 25.0x FY28E exit multiple for Kross—a modest premium to Jamna Auto's 23.0x and a clear premium to GNA Axles' 17.2x—is explicitly conditional on seamless tube backward integration lifting EBITDA margins by +150–200 bps and ROCE recovering above 20%. That conditionality is why our ₹268.00–₹282.00 pullback trigger is dual-gated on Q3 FY27 working-capital stabilization (<105 days) and February–March 2027 seamless tube trials staying on track. Until cash conversion shows up in filings, 25.0x is our ceiling rather than a 35x compounder multiple.

Capital return highlights the same contrast. Jamna Auto pays a 1.68% dividend yield with 26.0% ROCE at 23.0x Screener P/E (25.46x TradingView TTM) [26]. Kross is still raising debt and equity to build its tube mill at 28.42x TTM P/E [23]. Until free cash flow turns positive, Kross's valuation ceiling rests on plant execution.

Valuation Decision Trigger: We consider new capital only if Kross pulls back into ₹268.00–₹282.00 (1.69:1 asymmetry to ₹400.00 against the ₹212.00 stop) WITH Q3 FY27 working capital < 105 days or Feb–Mar 2027 seamless tube trials on track. A decisive close below ₹212.00 invalidates the Stage 2 thesis.

book_paragraphs: For six chapters, you and I deliberately refused to look at a single stock quote. We examined Kross Limited’s five Jamshedpur plants, its single-piece extruded trailer axles, its 124-day working capital cycle, and its -₹111 Cr three-year free cash flow without letting market sentiment color our judgment. Now that we know what the business actually is—a capable, backward-integrated Tier-1 manufacturer carrying real cyclicality and customer concentration—we can capture the stock price and ask a sharper question: what is the market assuming at ₹305.90?

On November 13, 2026, Kross closed at ₹305.90, giving the company a market capitalization of ₹1,970.44 Cr. That price represents 28.42x trailing-twelve-month earnings on TradingView (29.1x on Screener) and 3.77x book value of ₹81.10 per share. If you glance back at the 52-week range, the stock has doubled from its ₹150.52 low and sits only 6.28% below its ₹326.40 high after rallying 51.06% in three months. Why did buyers bid the stock up so fast? Because Q2 FY27 revenue jumped 79.6% year over year to ₹235.1 Cr and net profit surged 143.5% to ₹19.69 Cr, convincing momentum investors that a major earnings inflection has arrived.

book_subsections.title: What Reverse DCF Tells Us About Market Expectations
paragraphs: Whenever a cyclical stock rallies 51% in ninety days, you should flip the valuation problem upside down. Instead of asking what you think the stock is worth, ask what future operating performance ₹305.90 already demands. Adding ₹119 Cr of September 2026 borrowings to the ₹1,970.44 Cr equity value puts enterprise value near ₹2,060 Cr after netting operational cash. Using a 12.5% cost of capital and a 5% terminal growth rate, today’s price implies that Kross compounds revenue at roughly 16% to 18% a year through FY32 while lifting operating margins from the current 12%–13% band toward 15%–16%.

Pause and connect that math back to Chapter 3 and Chapter 6. For Kross to justify that trajectory on a cash-flow basis, two things must happen on schedule: first, the ₹167 Cr seamless tube plant must complete its February–March 2027 trials and lift EBITDA margins by 150 to 200 basis points (with full-ramp potential toward 300–400 bps); second, working capital must shrink from 124 days back below 90 days so net profit finally converts into free cash flow. On the post-October 30, 2026 fully diluted share count of 6.75 Cr shares (6,60,09,422 basic shares plus 15 lakh promoter warrants, or 6,75,09,422 shares), our Base Case models ₹108 Cr of FY28E PAT—or ₹16.00 per diluted share—which at a 25.0x exit P/E supports a ₹400.00 fair value.

Now look at the asymmetry from today’s price. Against a ₹212.00 structural stop, buying at ₹305.90 risks ₹93.90 per share for ₹94.10 of Base Case upside to ₹400.00—a reward-to-risk ratio of just 1.00 to 1. In our Bear Case, if freight demand cools or tube-mill commissioning slips, FY28E earnings stall near ₹12.15 per diluted share and the multiple compresses to 16.0x, pulling the stock back to ₹195.00. At ₹305.90, you are paying for execution before the cash flow has arrived.

book_subsections.title: Standing Kross Next to Its Listed Peers
paragraphs: The peer table sharpens that conclusion even further. Look at Jamna Auto Industries, which commands a ₹5,953.78 Cr market cap, earns a 26.0% ROCE and 22.3% ROE, pays a 1.68% dividend yield, and trades at 23.0x Screener P/E (25.46x TradingView TTM). Or look at GNA Axles, which grows TTM revenue at 23.06% with a 0.19x debt-to-equity ratio, earns 14.3% ROCE, and trades at 17.2x TTM P/E. Kross is priced at 28.42x TTM earnings—a clear premium to both Jamna Auto and GNA Axles—even though Kross’s ROCE fell to 16.4% in FY26 and its three-year free cash flow is negative.

Why then do we model a 25.0x FY28E exit multiple for Kross—above GNA Axles at 17.2x and slightly above Jamna Auto at 23.0x? That 25.0x multiple is explicitly conditional on seamless tube backward integration lifting EBITDA margins by 150–200 basis points and lifting ROCE back above 20% in FY28. That is precisely why our ₹268.00–₹282.00 pullback trigger is dual-gated: we demand both price retracement (where Base Case asymmetry widens to 1.69 to 1) and fundamental confirmation via Q3 FY27 working-capital stabilization below 105 days or February–March 2027 seamless tube trials staying on track.

Let us test the valuation one step further by asking what happens if working capital improves faster than expected. Suppose Kross trims its cash-conversion cycle from 124 days back toward 85 days over the next six quarters while the seamless tube mill ramps toward 40,000 tonnes per annum. In that scenario, incremental return on invested capital on the ₹167 Cr tube plant could exceed 22%, narrowing the quality gap with Jamna Auto’s 26.0% ROCE.

Even then, discipline requires anchoring your multiple to cyclical reality rather than bull-market euphoria. Applying a 25.0x Base Case multiple to ₹16.00 of FY28E diluted EPS yields ₹400.00—healthy upside from the ₹268.00–₹282.00 support zone (1.69:1 asymmetry), but barely 1.00:1 reward-to-risk if you chase at ₹305.90.

Notice how clean the valuation math becomes when you anchor it to peers rather than hype. At 28.42x trailing earnings, Kross already trades at a premium to Jamna Auto (23.0x Screener / 25.46x TTM) and GNA Axles (17.2x), even though Jamna Auto earns a 26.0% ROCE and pays a 1.68% dividend.
Waiting for ₹268.00–₹282.00 narrows that valuation risk and gives you a 1.69:1 reward-to-risk ratio toward our ₹400.00 Base Case target.

By anchoring our Base Case target at ₹400.00 on 25.0x FY28E diluted earnings (₹16.00 EPS across 6.75 Cr shares) and demanding a dual-gated pullback to ₹268.00–₹282.00, we avoid paying a compounder multiple before free cash flow turns positive.

In practical terms, that means refusing to extrapolate Q2 FY27’s +79.6% revenue surge as a permanent baseline without watching how working capital behaves across the full fiscal year. When a stock trades at 28.42x trailing earnings in a cyclical industry, your margin of safety comes from buying near support rather than chasing breakouts.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Paying for Promises vs. Paying for Proof
book_callouts.quote: At 28.4x trailing earnings, the market is already giving Kross partial credit for its FY28 seamless tube plant. Disciplined buyers let the stock pull back to support before underwriting execution risk.
book_callouts.text: The difference between a 1.00:1 trade at ₹305.90 and a 1.69:1 trade at ₹282.00 is not trivia—it is the margin of safety that protects you if the February 2027 tube-mill trials take an extra two quarters.
